title: CBA pushes for 'level playing field'
full_text:
Commonwealth Bank is ratcheting up the pressure on financial regulators to rein in Macquarie's use of a corporate structure it alleges provides an unfair competitive advantage, after commissioning economic analysis to show how the arrangement supports Macquarie's rapid growth in mortgages and deposits.
The analysis by Mandala, obtained by The Australian Financial Review, questions whether the settings applied to Macquarie by the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority create an uneven playing field by allowing it to operate with a lower capital base than major banks. The structure - known as a "non-operating holding company", or NOHC - allows an APRA-regulated bank to put businesses that do not involve holding deposits into a non-bank entity with lighter regulation. Macquarie created its NOHC in 2007.
The idea behind separating banking and non-bank businesses is to give the latter more flexibility to compete with players that are not prudentially regulated, such as private equity firms.
However, Mandala argues the structure has allowed Macquarie's banking operations to report a common equity tier 1 capital ratio - a key measure of a bank's financial security - that understates its true risk exposure.
That's because some of its risky investment, trading and asset management activity occurs in the non-bank group, which is excluded from CET1 capital calculations.
